items.title: WebAssembly's wasm2c sandbox escape. An untrusted WebAssembly module breaks out of the generated C sandbox and executes an arbitrary shell command on the host.
items.one_liner: This is a critical sandbox escape in a common Wasm-to-C compiler that allows RCE via memory corruption.
items.summary: A sandbox escape vulnerability in WebAssembly's wasm2c tool allows an untrusted module to execute arbitrary shell commands on a host. The flaw exists in wasm_rt_allocate_funcref_table(), where a failed calloc() allocation for a table is ignored, leaving the table with a NULL data pointer but a full declared size. This allows a guest to force an allocation failure by declaring a massive table, causing bounds checks to pass and table indices to be treated as absolute addresses. The attacker can then leak the libc address via the GOT and call system() to execute commands, verified on Linux arm64 and amd64.
key_facts: Mechanism: calloc() failure leading to NULL pointer dereference as absolute address
items.bottom_line: Untrusted WebAssembly modules compiled with wasm2c can break out of their sandbox and execute arbitrary code on the host system.

claims.text: The vulnerability allows an untrusted Wasm module to execute arbitrary shell commands.
claims.support_span: An untrusted WebAssembly module breaks out of the generated C sandbox and executes an arbitrary shell command on the host.

claims.text: The bug is caused by ignoring the result of calloc().
claims.support_span: wasm_rt_allocate_funcref_table() in wasm2c/wasm-rt-impl-tableops.inc sets table->size from the module's declared element count and then ignores the result of calloc().

claims.text: The exploit leaks the libc address using the GOT.
claims.support_span: table.get atgot_slot/32 reads the embedder's GOT through the broken table andtable.set stores the result into the module's own globals, where wasm code can read it as an integer. That leaks libc'smalloc address

items.title: Unpatched Magento and Adobe Commerce Zero-Day Exploited to Backdoor Online Stores
items.one_liner: An unpatched zero-day in Magento and Adobe Commerce is being exploited to gain remote code execution, with no official fix currently available.
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce, dubbed 'StyleSmuggler,' is being actively exploited to backdoor online stores. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server, and researchers report that patching status is currently irrelevant as the exploit bypasses existing security measures. Adobe has not yet released a patch or CVE identifier, leading security firms to recommend temporarily disabling GraphQL as a mitigation. Multiple stores have already been compromised, with attackers installing persistent backdoors.
items.bottom_line: If you run Magento or Adobe Commerce, you are currently vulnerable to unauthenticated RCE; disable GraphQL immediately if you do not rely on it for your storefront.
